title: Aioli
subtitle: Provencal garlic mayonnaise
excerpt: A thick, powerfully garlicky mayonnaise from Provence, made by emulsifying olive oil with raw garlic and egg yolk. Serve with crudites, grilled fish, or boiled vegetables.

recipe.sourceNotes: Aioli (from the Occitan ail, garlic, and oli, oil) is the great condiment of Provence in southern France and the Catalan regions of Spain. In its original form it is made without egg, using only raw garlic pounded to a paste with salt, and olive oil emulsified into the garlic paste by hand in a mortar: a technically demanding method that relies on the garlic's own emulsifying properties. The egg yolk version is an easier, more stable emulsion and is the form most commonly made at home outside the traditional regions. The authentic Provencal version has a stronger, more pungent flavour. Le grand aioli is a Provencal feast in which aioli is served with a variety of boiled and raw vegetables, hard-boiled eggs, salt cod, and snails. In modern British and American restaurant usage, the word aioli is often used loosely to mean flavoured mayonnaise, which is not the same thing.

content.text: All ingredients must be at room temperature before starting. Cold egg yolks and cold oil do not emulsify readily. Begin by pounding the garlic with the salt to a very smooth paste in a mortar, or mashing on a board with the flat of a knife. The oil must be added in a very thin trickle at the start; once the emulsion is established and the sauce is thick, the oil can be added in a slightly faster stream. If the aioli breaks, start with a fresh yolk in a clean bowl and whisk the broken aioli into it drop by drop.

items.preparation: pounded to a smooth paste with a little salt

content.text: Whisk the egg yolks, garlic paste, and mustard together in a bowl until combined. Begin adding the olive oil drop by drop, whisking constantly. The mixture will begin to thicken and turn pale as the emulsion forms.
Once the emulsion is established and the sauce is thick, add the oil in a thin but steady stream, still whisking constantly. The aioli should be very thick and hold its shape.
Season with lemon juice and salt. Taste: the aioli should be robustly garlicky. It will keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, covered. Serve at room temperature.
